air_operations_summary.air_superiority: Axis - Luftwaffe Bf 109 and Ju 87 dominated the battlefield

impact_on_ground_operations.allied: Limited close air support due to distance. RAF fighters unable to establish air superiority over battle area. Blenheim bombers suffered heavy losses.
impact_on_ground_operations.axis: Ju 87 Stukas provided devastating close air support. Bf 109 fighters prevented effective RAF intervention. German air superiority allowed Rommel to maneuver freely.

notable_engagements: Ju 87 Stukas attacked British armor columns - inflicted casualties and psychological impact
Bf 109 vs Hurricane/Tomahawk dogfights - German advantage in performance and pilot experience
RAF Blenheims attempted tactical bombing of Axis positions - heavy losses to fighters and flak

key_factors: Luftwaffe forward airfields enabled 3:1 sortie rate advantage
Bf 109E-7 superior to Hurricane Mk I in performance
Ju 87 Stuka proved highly effective against British armor
RAF handicapped by 200km+ distance to bases
Luftwaffe-Wehrmacht coordination more effective than RAF-Army
historical_assessment.impact_on_battle: Axis air superiority was a major factor in British defeat. Stuka attacks disrupted British armor formations, and Bf 109 prevented RAF close air support. British tanks attacked without effective air cover.
